target_customer: HR and people leaders at mid and large enterprises, mainly in India, Southeast Asia and the US
problem: Employees often feel unheard and hold back honest feedback, so companies learn about culture and attrition risk too late from annual surveys.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for an employee experience platform built around the Amber conversational AI
product_category: Employee experience and engagement software with conversational AI

founders.name: Tanmaya Jain
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2022-03-14) says the idea began when he and Varun Puri were still in school. No education details found.

founders.name: Varun Puri
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as running product, design and engineering. Named as co-founder by TechCrunch.

competitors.name: Peakon
competitors.what: Employee survey and engagement platform for employee retention
competitors.traction_then: Not stated in the cited snippets
competitors.funding_then: $22M Series B in February 2018 plus a $35M extension led by Atomico in March 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Conversational bot with multilingual support (TechCrunch cites more than 100 languages in 2022) and attrition prediction; standard NLP engineering with some hard parts, built by a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Survey and engagement tools are widely available. Employee conversation data and HR system integrations add switching costs once deployed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded engagement vendors already existed in 2020. No source shows one copying the Amber chatbot approach, and inFeedo raised a $12M Series A in March 2022.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reports 175 enterprise clients across 60 countries by March 2022, including Samsung, Xiaomi, Lenovo and TATA, and the founders say employees often do not give managers honest feedback.

branding.domain_note: Moved to infeedo.ai, consistent with the AI positioning.

identity.logo: inFeedo AI with a trademark mark
identity.mascot_or_character: Amber, a female conversational AI persona presented as a Chief Listening Officer
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and people first; the persona is named so employees talk to her like a colleague

branding.brand_signature: Amber, the AI Chief Listening Officer

brand_strength.rationale: The Amber persona is a distinctive product brand and the company explains its naming criteria (neutral across geographies, easy to spell, two syllables), but no sources show viral or community pull.

pivots.to: Focus on the Amber AI chatbot
pivots.why: A search summary says the company refocused on its core chatbot after finding regular employee input hard to maintain; not verified at the primary source

outcome_analysis: inFeedo moved from a 2017 seed to a $12M Series A in March 2022 led by Jungle Ventures with Tiger Global and Bling Capital, and TechCrunch reports 175 enterprise clients in 60 countries and about $16M raised in total. It sells to enterprises in Asia where it built a sales motion around the Amber bot, against better funded global rivals such as Peakon. Still active in 2026 with no acquisition or shutdown found.
notes: TechCrunch says about $16M total, so about $4M beyond the $12M Series A is unaccounted. The 2017 seed amount conflicts across outlets ($100,000, Rs 75 lakh, $150,000 angel); People Matters called it undisclosed, so the amount is left null. The 2020 YC and angel round amount is not stated. Founding year conflict: most sources say 2016, one profile says the older inFeedo began in 2013. The 2017 pivot and the 2017 seed come from search result summaries, not opened pages. Outcome search found no layoffs, shutdown or acquisition. Founder education and prior employers not found. Qualtrics and Culture Amp are named as takeover risk but not recorded as dated competitors because no dated source was found.
